objects: a two-dimensional table X in R^(SxC), where S is the number of image patches and C is the hidden channel dimension
assumptions: all image patches are linearly projected with the same shared projection matrix
no explicit position embeddings are used
guarantees: no formal theorem, lemma, or proof is provided for the architecture
empirical: 87.94% top-1 validation accuracy on ImageNet when pre-trained on JFT-300M
formalism.operation: alternately apply a token-mixing MLP across patches and a channel-mixing MLP across features of a fixed table

data_modalities: images split into fixed-size non-overlapping patches

evidence_spans.objects: Mixer takes as input a sequence of S non-overlapping image patches, each one projected to a desired hidden dimension C.
evidence_spans.assumptions: Unlike ViTs, Mixer does not use position embeddings because the token-mixing MLPs are sensitive to the order of the input tokens.
evidence_spans.guarantees: When pre-trained on large datasets, Mixer reaches near state-of-the-art performance... including 87.94% top-1 validation accuracy on ImageNet.
